name: intraday_trend_following_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms are working directional orders over 10-20 minute windows, they create a persistent EMA alignment visible as the 2-minute EMA sustaining itself above the 10-minute EMA. Brief pullbacks to the 2-minute EMA represent moments where short-term momentum sellers exhaust against resting institutional limit bids placed just below the recent micro-mean. At 5-second resolution, we detect the precise bar where NIFTY close returns above EMA(24) after the dip — signaling the institutional absorption has re-engaged — and ride the next 8-15 NIFTY spot points of continuation before the institutional order fill cycle completes.

indicators.name: ema_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute EMA as the pullback detection level and bounce entry trigger. Original used EMA(20) on 1-min = 20-min trend. Compressed to 2 min here because we hold 15-90s: a 2-min EMA reflects the micro-trend the trade rides; longer (e.g., 5-min EMA) would cause the pullback touch to be too deep relative to our 90s hold time, while shorter (1-min EMA) generates too many false touches from 5s noise.

indicators.name: ema_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute EMA as the trend direction context filter. Original used EMA(50) on 1-min = 50-min trend. Shortened from 50 min to 10 min because 50-min trend direction is too stale for a 15-90s trade — a NIFTY trend established 40 minutes ago is irrelevant to the next 30 seconds. 10 min captures the current intraday directional bias without including pre-session gap effects, and produces 3-8 valid aligned states per day.

indicators.name: rsi_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute RSI to prevent entries into exhausted short-term moves. Matched to EMA(24) window for consistency. Avoids entering a CE when the 2-min momentum is already extended (RSI > 65) — on NIFTY, an RSI above 65 over 2 minutes typically means the immediate burst is 70-80% complete and a counter-move is imminent.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP as institutional price anchor — no scaling needed, cumulative from open. Confirms NIFTY is on the correct side of the institutional benchmark before entry. Eliminates trades where the pullback is actually a mean-reversion toward VWAP rather than a micro-pullback in a trend above it.

conditions: EMA(24) > EMA(120) by at least trend_strength_pct (bullish trend aligned)
Previous bar: low <= EMA(24) * (1 + pullback_tolerance) — bar dipped to EMA(24)
Current bar: close > EMA(24) — bounce confirmed above EMA(24)
close > VWAP — above session institutional anchor
buy_ce.confirmation: Bar closes above EMA(24) after previous bar touched it

conditions: EMA(24) < EMA(120) by at least trend_strength_pct (bearish trend aligned)
Previous bar: high >= EMA(24) * (1 - pullback_tolerance) — bar rallied to EMA(24)
Current bar: close < EMA(24) — rejection confirmed below EMA(24)
close < VWAP — below session institutional anchor
buy_pe.confirmation: Bar closes below EMA(24) after previous bar touched it

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points (~6 NIFTY spot points at delta ~0.5): if the EMA(24) bounce fails and NIFTY retraces 6 spot points from entry within 15 seconds, the institutional bid is NOT absorbing selling and the micro-trend has already reversed — waiting longer increases loss without thesis support. Consistent with 15-30s NIFTY typical adverse move of 2-5 spot pts; 6 pts is the outer edge of normal noise.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option points (~10 NIFTY spot points): EMA(24) pullback continuations on NIFTY carry 10-15 spot points in the next 30-90 seconds when the trend is genuine. Targeting 10 spot pts captures ~70% of the expected continuation leg and exits well before the next EMA touch. R:R = 1:1.67 at 3-pt stop.

filters.vix_filter: none — VIX not used; trend_strength_pct implicitly filters choppy low-volatility days where EMA alignment is unstable
filters.time_filter: 09:35-15:20 IST — skip first 20 min for trend to establish, no late entries
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume at 5s is noisy; VWAP position acts as implicit volume/conviction filter
filters.trend_filter: EMA(24) vs EMA(120) separation > trend_strength_pct is the trend filter
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — institutional trend-following algorithms on NIFTY are structural and persistent; the EMA pullback entry pattern reflects a stable microstructure dynamic

adaptation_notes: Original used EMA(20/50) on 1-min bars with universe of 25 NIFTY50 stocks, ADX(14) filter, and stock-specific filters (results day, turnover rank). All stock-specific elements are dropped for the NIFTY index. ADX(14) is replaced by the EMA separation ratio (EMA24 vs EMA120) as a trend strength proxy — ADX on 5s bars is too noisy. Lookbacks are NOT 12x scaled: EMA(20min→2min) and EMA(50min→10min) because hold time compresses from 20-90 min to 15-90 seconds, requiring proportionally tighter trigger and context windows. RSI(14min→2min) matched to EMA(24) window. VWAP unchanged (cumulative). Pullback tolerance replaces 'low <= EMA_20 * 1.001' with a tunable threshold.
weaknesses: EMA(24) on 5s bars is sensitive to single-tick spikes — a brief 5s dip to EMA24 can trigger without genuine institutional demand absorption
On days where NIFTY gaps and trends all day, EMA(24) rarely touches, producing very few signals
EMA(120) separation threshold may miss early-stage trends that are nascent but not yet showing >0.1% separation
